sourcedFrom: Ruger Silent-SR Sound Suppressor Instruction Manual — PM386 (undated on cover)
cleanIntro: A serviceable rimfire can: it comes apart, and it is meant to. Ruger’s own caution comes first — do not open a dirty suppressor unless you are going to finish the job.

steps.title: Host clear, and commit to finishing
steps.action: Clear the host firearm completely first. Then decide: once this can is open you are cleaning it.
steps.prose: Ruger states this outright, in capitals. A part-cleaned can reassembled dirty is worse than one left alone.
steps.quote: DO NOT DISASSEMBLE A DIRTY SUPPRESSOR UNLESS YOU PLAN ON CLEANING IT.
steps.cite: Ruger Silent-SR Sound Suppressor Instruction Manual — PM386 — Cleaning, p.8
steps.warn: Once fired, suppressors contain a great deal of lead residue.

steps.title: End caps off
steps.action: Using the provided disassembly tool, remove the front and rear caps.
steps.prose: The tool that came with the can is the tool for the job — the caps are thin-walled and a wrench marks them.
steps.quote: Using the provided disassembly tool, remove the front and rear caps.
steps.cite: Ruger Silent-SR Sound Suppressor Instruction Manual — PM386 — Disassembly, step 1, p.7

steps.title: Baffle stack out
steps.action: Slide the entire baffle stack out of the rear of the suppressor tube. If it is stubborn, tap or push it through with a wooden dowel.
steps.prose: Wooden, so nothing steel touches the baffles or the bore of the tube.
steps.quote: Slide the entire stack of baffles out of the rear of the suppressor tube. If necessary, you may tap or push the baffle stack with a wooden dowel.
steps.cite: Ruger Silent-SR Sound Suppressor Instruction Manual — PM386 — Disassembly, step 2, p.7

steps.title: Separate the baffles — keep the order
steps.action: Snap each baffle apart from the next, by hand where you can. A hex key or punch in the apertures will pry them apart if carbon has locked them.
steps.prose: Lay them out in the order they came off. Baffles are directional and the stack goes back the way it came.
steps.quote: Each component of the baffle stack will need to be snapped apart from the others.
steps.cite: Ruger Silent-SR Sound Suppressor Instruction Manual — PM386 — Disassembly, step 3, p.7

deepAbsentReason: The Silent-SR baffle strip IS the full disassembly Ruger documents — caps off, stack out, baffles separated. There is no further level published, so this listing has NO deep clean.

cleaning.name: BAFFLES
tasks: Clean each baffle individually with a solvent suited to lead and carbon
Work wet and wear gloves — a fired can holds a great deal of lead residue
Keep the stack in order as you clean; baffles are directional

cleaning.name: TUBE & REAR CAP — MATERIAL LIMITS
tasks: The tube is titanium and the rear cap aluminum
Do NOT ultrasonically clean these, and do not scrub them with a steel brush
Do not use chemicals corrosive to aluminum or titanium
A soft brass, plastic or cotton brush is what Ruger permits

reassembly: Reassemble the baffle stack in its original order and orientation.
Slide the stack back into the tube and fit both caps with the provided tool.
fncheck: With the can reassembled, sight through the bore path against the light — daylight straight and centred — before it goes back on a host.
